Please Don’t Blur Scripture and Tradition. I have genuinely enjoyed many of Duomo’s Bible studies. They are thoughtful, engaging, and have encouraged me to spend more time in Scripture.

However, I was surprised to find “Rosary Prayers” included in what is presented as a Bible study app. I understand that the opening words of the Hail Mary come from Luke’s Gospel, but the prayer continues with, “Holy Mary… pray for us sinners,” which is part of Catholic tradition and is not taught as a Christian prayer in the New Testament.

My concern is not about criticizing any Christian tradition. My concern is about clarity. A Bible study app should clearly distinguish between what is taught in Scripture and what belongs to a particular church tradition.

Many Christians download an app like this because they are looking for Bible-based teaching. When Scripture and tradition are presented together without a clear distinction, it can create confusion and cause users like me to question the app’s doctrinal foundation.

I hope the Duomo team will consider making that distinction more explicit. Greater transparency would build trust and help users study God’s Word with confidence.
